systemMemoryValidation.guard: tests/m2-bounded.py dynamically uses Windows-reported physical memory and retains the Windows Job timeout and cleanup
systemMemoryValidation.nodeHeap: The guard requests a system-sized Node old-space limit; a direct verification reported 34160508928 bytes for Node's effective heap limit under the 34110816256-byte job limit.
systemMemoryValidation.browserSetting: M2 browser drivers request an old-space limit equal to reported system memory
systemMemoryValidation.limitations: The large system-memory run preceded the guard's added Node heap option; the final component replay exercised that option. The browser reports a smaller JavaScript heap limit than the requested physical-memory setting. These runs do not establish general resource reliability.

subsequentChromeHeapControl.method: Fresh headless Chrome pages requested 512 MiB and 32530 MiB with --js-flags=max-old-space-size. performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit was read in non-cross-origin-isolated pages, so values are rounded.
subsequentChromeHeapControl.interpretation: The system-sized request is passed to Chrome, but the browser reports a substantially lower JavaScript heap ceiling. This is separate from the system-sized Windows Job limit and does not limit total process memory to the JavaScript heap size.
subsequentChromeHeapControl.limitation: V8 source describes a compressed-pointer allocator constraint; this control does not inspect the installed Chrome build configuration or prove its exact limiting mechanism.
